items.description: Stuck on a configuration, wondering why a device will not pair, or just want to see what other people are building? Home Assistant has one of the most active home-automation communities on the internet, and most of it is free to join. The official channels are below; further down you will find communities in your language and around specific projects from the wider ecosystem.
items.title: In case you need help

items.description: Discords, forums, and chats run by community projects you will see elsewhere on this list. Sorted alphabetically by project.

items.title: Frigate Discussions

items.title: Zigbee2MQTT Discussions

items.description: Home Assistant is not the only home-automation platform out there. If you want to compare, or if you have specific needs Home Assistant does not cover, the projects below are the most active alternatives. Some are commercial, some are open source, and a few solve very different problems.

items.title: Homebridge
items.description: Lightweight Node.js server that bridges non-HomeKit devices into Apple Home, with a large plugin ecosystem (25,384★).

items.title: Node-RED
items.description: Flow-based visual programming tool for wiring together devices, APIs, and services, backed by the OpenJS Foundation (23,277★).

items.title: Domoticz
items.description: A lightweight Home Automation System (3,773★).

items.title: Gladys
items.description: Open source program which runs on your Raspberry Pi (3,066★).

items.title: ioBroker
items.description: Integration platform for IoT with hundreds of adapters and strong European protocol support for KNX and HomeMatic (1,371★).

items.title: Jeedom
items.description: French-origin, cloudless platform with a plugin marketplace, running on any Linux system (414★).
